claim.statement: The v37 May 2 xPool follow-up did not show a clean independent worker, teacher, or retiree action cluster: the job completed 10 pages with 62 emitted items, 61 usable texts, 34 teacher-coded posts, 26 worker-coded posts, no retiree-coded posts, and only 2 posts with protest/strike/gathering terms; manual inspection found Teacher Day tribute/loyalty/martyr language and worker memorial/commentary rather than source-near strike or gathering evidence.
claim.subject: Persian X labor and Teacher Day discourse after May 2
claim.object: ceremony, loyalty, memorial, and commentary heavy rather than verified independent action

evidence.summary: The saved xPool result completed 10 pages, emitted 62 items, and stopped at MAX_PAGES_REACHED for a May 2 Persian labor/teacher/retiree query.
The notes record keyword coding of 61 usable texts and manual inspection showing tribute, loyalty, and memorial discourse without a clean source-near strike or gathering cluster.

information_depth.rationale: The saved sample is useful for visible discourse topology and bounded negative evidence, but xPool cannot observe suppressed offline action or private coordination.

assessment.uncertainty: A later teacher-council, worker, retiree, family, or local video source could overturn the no-clean-cluster read.

claim.statement: The May 2 follow-up keeps May Day and Teacher Day grievances inside formal or managed channels: current worker evidence remains the ILNA/Rokna job-security, Social Security, inspection, livelihood, inflation, and retiree-support demand lane, while teacher evidence remains ceremony, gifts/payments, Keshvar-Doust allegiance framing, and known repression cases rather than verified independent coordination.

claim.object: formal worker demands and managed teacher ceremony rather than verified independent coordination

evidence.summary: The notes record that Exa follow-up results were mostly ceremonies, official programs, managed payments, formal worker demand channels, or stale retiree results, not source-near independent action.
ILNA reported West Azerbaijan laid-off workers asking for job security and real support instead of ceremonial May Day greetings.
Rokna/Vista carried the House Worker May Day resolution packaging demands through a formal labor channel.
SNN announced a state-aligned Keshvar-Doust Teacher Day gathering framed around allegiance and resistance language.
Sedaye Mardom's Kerman teacher-repression report shows coercion beneath Teacher Day ceremony, but not a new May 2 action cluster.

information_depth.rationale: The claim reuses canonical domestic labor and teacher rows and adds a focused follow-up search/social pass.

assessment.uncertainty: Negative evidence is bounded by blackout and sampling limits; follow-up should watch May 3-7.

claim.statement: IranWire's May Day interview frames the Dey 1404 crackdown as a labor-class trauma and organizing problem: Foad Keykhosravi said the protests began from livelihood pressure, quickly became workforce-heavy, that close to 500 dead workforce members had been documented before the internet cutoff, and that the missing ingredient is independent networked social organization.
claim.subject: Dey 1404 labor protest memory
claim.object: worker-class trauma plus independent organizing gap

evidence.summary: IranWire interviewed labor organizer Foad Keykhosravi, who described Dey protests as livelihood-origin and workforce-heavy, cited close to 500 documented workforce deaths before the internet cutoff, and emphasized networked organization.

information_depth.rationale: The source is a current interview and useful strategic context, but the death count is an organizer/research claim requiring direct underlying dataset access.

assessment.uncertainty: Treat the near-500 workforce-death figure as attributed to the interviewee until the underlying Pezhvak/Confederation documentation is obtained.

synthesis.title: Cracks in the Islamic Republic, v37 - labor and teacher anger stays managed on May 2
synthesis.summary: The thirty-seventh pass answers the immediate May Day / Teacher Day follow-up toward containment, not crossover. The worker lane is still hard-edged but formal: ILNA and House Worker/Rokna put job security, layoffs, Social Security, inspection, livelihood, inflation, and retiree support into demand language, but v37 did not find a fresh source-near post-May-2 strike or worker gathering cluster. The teacher lane is still a split screen: public output is `#سپاس_معلم`, Teacher Day congratulations, war-martyr teacher commemoration, managed gift/payment texture, and a Keshvar-Doust allegiance gathering, while prior rows still show Kerman teacher activists facing prison/fines and pay/pension grievances underneath. The new xPool sample is useful negative evidence: 62 items, 61 usable texts, 34 teacher-coded, 26 worker-coded, no retiree-coded posts, and only 2 protest/strike/gathering-coded posts. IranWire adds why this remains latent rather than resolved: the Dey 1404 worker-death memory is heavy, but the same interview identifies independent networked organization as the missing ingredient. Net: labor and teacher anger is real, but visible May 2 follow-up stays in formal, loyal, memorial, and managed channels rather than verified independent coordination.
synthesis.limitations: This is bounded negative evidence under blackout and heavy propaganda/ceremony conditions. xPool is not representative, Exa may miss local offline action, and stale aggregator wrappers can look current. Treat the May 2 read as a live containment snapshot, not proof that labor/teacher coordination cannot emerge. Follow May 3-7 for repeat retiree gatherings, teacher-council statements, local school action, unemployment-insurance complaints, and whether loyalty events generate counter-mobilization.

information_depth.rationale: The synthesis combines existing canonical labor/teacher rows, fresh Exa source hygiene, a completed xPool sample, and IranWire labor-organizing context.

operations.rationale: The May 2 xPool sample directly tests whether visible worker, teacher, or retiree discourse shows independent coordination after the ceremony window.

Formal worker and teacher channels currently keep economic grievances in a lawful/managed frame while repression defines the boundary.
The IranWire interview frames labor as central to Dey protests but identifies the lack of networked organization as the barrier to durable coordination.
The interview links worker deaths, unemployment, inflation, internet/business collapse, and organizing capacity to the risk of a delayed labor-protest wave.
